topic: Loan at "1% a month": why a flat rate is really ~21% a year
hook_pattern: contrarian-number (1% a month flat isn't 12% a year)
caption:
"Just 1% a month" sounds like 12% a year. On a flat-rate loan, it isn't.

A flat rate charges interest on the full amount you borrowed for the whole term, even as your EMIs pay it down. Illustrative example: ₹1 lakh at 1% a month flat for 3 years means ₹36,000 of interest and an EMI of about ₹3,778. Measured on the reducing balance, the way most loans are quoted, that's roughly 21% a year, not 12%. Processing fees push the real cost higher still.

Before you sign:
1. Ask whether the rate is flat or reducing-balance.
2. Read the APR (annual percentage rate) in the Key Fact Statement. RBI has required lenders to give one, with an all-inclusive APR, for retail and MSME term loans since 1 Oct 2024.
3. Compare loans by APR, not by the monthly rate.

Save this for the next time someone quotes you a monthly rate. Ever been quoted a flat rate?

Sources: Wikipedia, "Flat rate (finance)"; Vinod Kothari Consultants and Outlook Money on RBI's Key Fact Statement rules (Apr 2024). Rupee figures and the ~21% rate are our illustrative calculations.
